question: What is India’s average annual HDI growth for the period 1990-2019?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1.42**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's average annual Human Development Index (HDI) growth rate from 1990 to 2019 is **1.42%**.
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary measure of average achievement in key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, being knowledgeable, and having a decent standard of living.
 
• India's HDI value for 2019 was **0.645**, placing it in the medium human development category.
 
• The growth in HDI reflects improvements in life expectancy, education, and per capita income levels over the years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**

 
 
• Developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and published annually.
 
• It measures and ranks countries' levels of social and economic development based on life expectancy, education, and per capita income indicators.
 
• Countries are classified into four tiers: very high, high, medium, and low human development.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy**
 
 
• It is the average number of years a person is expected to live based on the year of their birth, current age, and other demographic factors.
 
• Life expectancy at birth is a key component of the HDI.
 
 
 
• **Education Index**
 
 
• It is calculated using the mean years of schooling for adults aged 25 years and more and the expected years of schooling for children of school-entry age.
 
• This index is a crucial indicator in measuring the education dimension of the HDI.
 
 
 
• **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**
 
 
• It is the total domestic and foreign output claimed by residents of a country, divided by the population.
 
• GNI per capita is used to measure the standard of living and is a key part of the HDI calculation.
